title: Token-drift trajectory probes land as agentic-coherence audit primitive by Q4 2026
body: By Q4 2026 the token-drift trajectory mapping primitive introduced Thursday on arxiv.org/abs/2605.11823 by CMU Catalyst PhD candidate Tianqi Chen, Meta FAIR senior research scientist Naman Goyal, and Catalyst lab director Zhihao Jia lands as a named auditable measurement instrument in at least three of the publicly tracked agentic-AI evaluation surfaces — the MLCommons AI Safety v1.2 benchmark working group, the NIST AI Safety Institute's Risk Management Framework Profile-1 long-horizon-agent annex, and the EU AI Act Article 15 conformity assessment harmonized standard CEN-CENELEC JTC 21 working draft — with the drift-magnitude threshold at the policy-divergence inflection adopted as the falsifiable measurement primitive for long-horizon agentic coherence failure characterization that all three working groups had been holding in pre-coverage limbo since the Q1 2026 NIST AISI public RFC closed on March 14 without a quantitative drift-probe candidate. The structural force is that token-drift trajectory mapping is the first probe instrument that ties a published 84.3 percent SWE-Bench Verified failure-mode prediction accuracy to a single drift-magnitude scalar measurable at audit-time without trainer-side cooperation, composing additively with the Stanford CRFM + DeepMind reservoir-routing primitive from Wednesday's arxiv 2605.10142 to lift the same 145B-parameter MoE backbone from 78.7 to 81.2 on SWE-Bench Verified — a fresh 2.5pp absolute lift on top of the reservoir-routing uplift while reducing per-turn router-compute cost by an additional 12.8 percent on the same 8x H100 SXM5 reference node — which gives the standards-track cohort the composition demonstration they had been waiting for to defend a probe primitive against the inevitable industry pushback that any safety-side instrument carries unbounded inference-cost overhead. Simon Willison's Thursday afternoon note flagging the paper as the second credible MoE-router primitive shipping inside 48 hours plus Hacker News's two independent CoreWeave H100 SXM5 reproductions inside 2.8 percent of the reference sheet establishes the reproducibility floor that NIST AISI's measurement-science branch requires before naming a probe in a formal annex, and the open Apache 2.0 reference implementation expected to land in the CMU Catalyst project repository inside the standard six-week post-arxiv release window crosses the open-implementation threshold that CEN-CENELEC JTC 21 working drafts use to classify a primitive as harmonized-standard-eligible rather than vendor-proprietary. The most likely landing is that by Q4 2026 the MLCommons AI Safety v1.2 benchmark publishes token-drift trajectory mapping as a named scoring dimension on its long-horizon-agent subtest, NIST AISI's RMF Profile-1 annex cites the drift-magnitude threshold at the policy-divergence inflection as the recommended measurement primitive for long-horizon agentic coherence failure characterization, and CEN-CENELEC JTC 21 incorporates the same drift-magnitude scalar into its conformity-assessment harmonized standard draft for EU AI Act Article 15 long-horizon-agent applicability. Bear case is that a competing fused-routing-context probe from a Big-3 hyperscaler research lab lands inside the same window with a higher SWE-Bench Verified failure-mode prediction accuracy and splits the standards-track cohort's primitive selection, slipping cross-standard adoption into Q1 2027; absent that fragmentation, Q4 2026 lands token-drift trajectory mapping as the first measurement-side agentic-AI audit primitive named across all three of the MLCommons, NIST AISI, and CEN-CENELEC JTC 21 standards surfaces.

reasoning.because: CMU Catalyst + Meta FAIR shipped a 84.3 percent accuracy drift probe on arxiv 2605.11823 today
reasoning.given: MLCommons, NIST AISI, and CEN-CENELEC JTC 21 each held probe selection open through Q1 2026 RFC cycles
reasoning.so_that: the composition uplift to 81.2 SWE-Bench Verified plus open Apache 2.0 reference clears standards-eligibility floors
reasoning.landing: Q4 2026 named adoption across MLCommons, NIST AISI, and CEN-CENELEC JTC 21 surfaces
reasoning.plain_language: A new way to measure when AI agents go off track will be written into AI safety rules by the end of 2026.

summary: A Thursday CMU Catalyst + Meta FAIR paper introduces token-drift trajectory mapping, a probe predicting agentic failure with 84.3 percent accuracy. By Q4 2026 the primitive lands as a named audit measurement across MLCommons AI Safety v1.2, NIST AISI RMF Profile-1, and the EU AI Act CEN-CENELEC JTC 21 harmonized standard.
